sanskrit: tāṃ dhṛtiṃ kuru rādheya tataḥ pratyehi pāṇḍavam vāsudevaṃ ca vārṣṇeyaṃ prīyamāṇaṃ kirīṭinā
english: Summon that same resolve, O Rādheya, and then go forth to meet the Pāṇḍava and Vāsudeva of the Vṛṣṇis, who rejoices in the Diademed One.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca prakṛtistho hi me śalya idānīṃ saṃmatas tathā pratibhāsi mahābāho vibhīś caiva dhanaṃjayāt
english: Karṇa said: Now, O Śalya, you appear to me restored to your true self and well-disposed, O mighty-armed one, and unafraid of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: paśya bāhvor balaṃ me 'dya śikṣitasya ca paśya me eko 'dya nihaniṣyāmi pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūm
english: Behold this day the strength of my arms, and behold my mastery of arms: alone today I shall destroy the great host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇau ca puruṣavyāghrau tac ca satyaṃ bravīmi te nāhatvā yudhi tau vīrāv apayāsye kathaṃ cana
english: And the two Kṛṣṇas, those tigers among men—this truth I tell you: never shall I withdraw without having slain those two heroes in battle.

sanskrit: svapsye vā nihatas tābhyām asatyo hi raṇe jayaḥ kṛtārtho vā bhaviṣyāmi hatvā tāv atha vā hataḥ
english: Either I shall lie slain by them in sleep—for victory in battle is never assured—or I shall achieve my purpose by killing them; otherwise I shall fall myself.

sanskrit: naitādṛśo jātu babhūva loke; rathottamo yāvad anuśrutaṃ naḥ tam īdṛśaṃ pratiyotsyāmi pārthaṃ; mahāhave paśya ca pauruṣaṃ me
english: Never in this world, as far as we have heard, has there been so peerless a chariot-warrior. Against such a Pārtha I shall fight in the great battle—behold then my manhood.

sanskrit: rathe caraty eṣa rathapravīraḥ; śīghrair hayaiḥ kauravarājaputraḥ sa vādya māṃ neṣyati kṛcchram etat; karṇasyāntād etad antāḥ stha sarve
english: This foremost of chariot-heroes ranges upon his car with swift horses, this prince of the Kuru kings. Either he shall bring me to grief this day, or else—mark this—the end of all of you lies in the end of Karṇa.

sanskrit: asvedinau rājaputrasya hastāv; avepinau jātakiṇau bṛhantau dṛḍhāyudhaḥ kṛtimān kṣiprahasto; na pāṇḍaveyena samo 'sti yodhaḥ
english: The prince's hands neither sweat nor tremble; they are broad and calloused with use. Firm in his weapon, skilled, swift of hand—there is no warrior equal to the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: gṛhṇāty anekān api kaṅkapatrān; ekaṃ yathā tān kṣitipān pramathya te krośamātraṃ nipatanty amoghāḥ; kas tena yodho 'sti samaḥ pṛthivyām
english: He grasps many heron-feathered shafts as though they were but one, and crushing the lords of earth those unerring arrows fall a full krośa away. What warrior on earth is his equal?

sanskrit: atoṣayat pāṇḍaveyo hutāśaṃ; kṛṣṇadvitīyo 'tirathas tarasvī lebhe cakraṃ yatra kṛṣṇo mahātmā; dhanur gāṇḍīvaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ savyasācī
english: The son of Pāṇḍu, that swift over-chariot-warrior with Kṛṣṇa for his second, gratified the Fire-eater—there the great-souled Kṛṣṇa won his discus, and the Pāṇḍava Savyasācin won the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: śvetāśvayuktaṃ ca sughoṣam agryaṃ; rathaṃ mahābāhur adīnasattvaḥ maheṣudhī cākṣayau divyarūpau; śastrāṇi divyāni ca havyavāhāt
english: From the Bearer of Oblations the mighty-armed one of undaunted spirit obtained that foremost chariot of fair thunder yoked with white horses, two great inexhaustible quivers of divine form, and divine weapons.

sanskrit: tathendraloke nijaghāna daityān; asaṃkhyeyān kālakeyāṃś ca sarvān lebhe śaṅkhaṃ devadattaṃ sma tatra; ko nāma tenābhyadhikaḥ pṛthivyām
english: So too in Indra's realm he slew countless Daityas and all the Kālakeyas, and there he won the conch named Devadatta. Who upon earth, then, is greater than he?

sanskrit: mahādevaṃ toṣayām āsa caiva; sākṣāt suyuddhena mahānubhāvaḥ lebhe tataḥ pāśupataṃ sughoraṃ; trailokyasaṃhārakaraṃ mahāstram
english: That man of mighty power gratified Mahādeva himself in fair combat face to face, and thereby won the dread Pāśupata, the great weapon that works the destruction of the three worlds.

sanskrit: pṛthak pṛthag lokapālāḥ sametā; dadur hy astrāṇy aprameyāṇi yasya yais tāñ jaghānāśu raṇe nṛsiṃhān; sa kālakhañjān asurān sametān
english: The guardians of the worlds, gathered together and each apart, gave him immeasurable weapons—with which that lion among men swiftly slew in battle the assembled Kālakhañja Asuras.

sanskrit: tathā virāṭasya pure sametān; sarvān asmān ekarathena jitvā jahāra tad godhanam ājimadhye; vastrāṇi cādatta mahārathebhyaḥ
english: And in the city of Virāṭa, with a single chariot, he conquered us all assembled there, carried off that wealth of cattle in the midst of battle, and stripped the garments from the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tam īdṛśaṃ vīryaguṇopapannaṃ; kṛṣṇadvitīyaṃ varaye raṇāya anantavīryeṇa ca keśavena; nārāyaṇenāpratimena guptam
english: Such a one, endowed with the virtues of valor, with Kṛṣṇa for his second, do I choose to fight—him guarded by Keśava of boundless might, by the matchless Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: varṣāyutair yasya guṇā na śakyā; vaktuṃ sametair api sarvalokaiḥ mahātmanaḥ śaṅkhacakrāsipāṇer; viṣṇor jiṣṇor vasudevātmajasya bhayaṃ me vai jāyate sādhvasaṃ ca; dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāv ekarathe sametau
english: The virtues of that great soul—conch, discus, and sword in hand, Viṣṇu the conqueror, son of Vasudeva—could not be told in ten thousand years even by all the worlds together. Fear indeed arises in me, and a shudder, to behold the two Kṛṣṇas joined upon a single car.

sanskrit: ubhau hi śūrau kṛtinau dṛḍhāstrau; mahārathau saṃhananopapannau etādṛśau phalgunavāsudevau; ko 'nyaḥ pratīyān mad ṛte nu śalya
english: Both are brave, accomplished, firm in their weapons, great chariot-warriors of well-knit frame. Against such as Phalguna and Vāsudeva, who other than I, O Śalya, would come forth?

sanskrit: etāv ahaṃ yudhi vā pātayiṣye; māṃ vā kṛṣṇau nihaniṣyato 'dya iti bruvañ śalyam amitrahantā; karṇo raṇe megha ivonnanāda
english: Either I shall lay these two low in battle, or the two Kṛṣṇas shall slay me this day. So speaking to Śalya, Karṇa the slayer of foes roared in the fight like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: abhyetya putreṇa tavābhinanditaḥ; sametya covāca kurupravīrān kṛpaṃ ca bhojaṃ ca mahābhujāv ubhau; tathaiva gāndhāranṛpaṃ sahānujam guroḥ sutaṃ cāvarajaṃ tathātmanaḥ; padātino 'tha dvipasādino 'nyān
english: Greeted with applause by your son when he drew near, he came together with the Kuru heroes and addressed them—Kṛpa and the Bhoja, both mighty-armed, the Gāndhāra king with his younger brothers, the preceptor's son, and his own younger brother, and others, the foot-soldiers and the elephant-riders:

sanskrit: nirundhatābhidravatācyutārjunau; śrameṇa saṃyojayatāśu sarvataḥ yathā bhavadbhir bhṛśavikṣatāv ubhau; sukhena hanyām aham adya bhūmipāḥ
english: "Hem them in, charge upon Acyuta and Arjuna, wear them down at once on every side with toil, that when both have been sorely wounded by you, O lords of earth, I may slay them with ease this day."

sanskrit: tatheti coktvā tvaritāḥ sma te 'rjunaṃ; jighāṃsavo vīratamāḥ samabhyayuḥ nadīnadān bhūrijalo mahārṇavo; yathā tathā tān samare 'rjuno 'grasat
english: Saying "So be it," those bravest of the brave swiftly bore down upon Arjuna, eager to slay him; but as the great brimming ocean swallows the rivers and streams, so did Arjuna swallow them up in battle.

sanskrit: na saṃdadhāno na tathā śarottamān; pramuñcamāno ripubhiḥ pradṛśyate dhanaṃjayas tasya śaraiś ca dāritā; hatāś ca petur naravājikuñjarāḥ
english: Neither in the nocking nor in the loosing of his finest shafts could Dhanaṃjaya be seen by his foes; and torn and slain by his arrows there fell men, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: śarārciṣaṃ gāṇḍivacārumaṇḍalaṃ; yugāntasūryapratimānatejasam na kauravāḥ śekur udīkṣituṃ jayaṃ; yathā raviṃ vyādhitacakṣuṣo janāḥ
english: Flaming with arrows, his Gāṇḍīva drawn to a fair full circle, blazing with splendor like the sun at the dissolution of the age—the Kauravas could no more bear to gaze on the victor than men with diseased eyes can look upon the sun.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvad visṛjañ śarān kṛpas; tathaiva bhojas tava cātmajaḥ svayam jighāṃsubhis tān kuśalaiḥ śarottamān; mahāhave saṃjavitān prayatnataḥ śaraiḥ praciccheda ca pāṇḍavas tvaran; parābhinad vakṣasi ca tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Kṛpa rushed upon him loosing arrows, and so too the Bhoja and your son himself; but in that great battle the Pāṇḍava, hastening, cut to pieces those finest shafts which they had sped with deadly care and effort, and pierced each of them through the breast with three arrows apiece.

sanskrit: sa gāṇḍivābhyāyatapūrṇamaṇḍalas; tapan ripūn arjunabhāskaro babhau śarograraśmiḥ śuciśukramadhyago; yathaiva sūryaḥ pariveṣagas tathā
english: With his Gāṇḍīva drawn to its full and ample circle, scorching his foes, Arjuna the sun shone forth—his rays the cruel arrows, ranging through the bright clear sky as the sun set within its halo.

sanskrit: athāgryabāṇair daśabhir dhanaṃjayaṃ; parābhinad droṇasuto 'cyutaṃ tribhiḥ caturbhir aśvāṃś caturaḥ kapiṃ tathā; śaraiḥ sa nārācavarair avākirat
english: Then Droṇa's son pierced Dhanaṃjaya with ten foremost arrows, Acyuta with three, the four horses with four, and the ape upon the banner he overwhelmed with choice iron shafts.

sanskrit: tathā tu tat tat sphurad āttakārmukaṃ; tribhiḥ śarair yantṛśiraḥ kṣureṇa hayāṃś caturbhiś caturas tribhir dhvajaṃ; dhanaṃjayo drauṇirathān nyapātayat
english: In return Dhanaṃjaya, with his quivering bow taken up, brought down from Droṇa's son's chariot his bow with three arrows, the driver's head with a razor-shaft, his four horses with four, and his banner with three.

sanskrit: sa roṣapūrṇo 'śanivajrahāṭakair; alaṃkṛtaṃ takṣakabhogavarcasam subandhanaṃ kārmukam anyad ādade; yathā mahāhipravaraṃ gires tathā
english: Filled with fury, he took up another bow, adorned with gold like lightning's bolt, gleaming like the coils of Takṣaka, well-strung—as one might lift a great serpent-king from a mountain.

sanskrit: svam āyudhaṃ copavikīrya bhūtale; dhanuś ca kṛtvā saguṇaṃ guṇādhikaḥ samānayānāv ajitau narottamau; śarottamair drauṇir avidhyad antikāt
english: Strewing his own broken weapon upon the ground and stringing his bow afresh, the son of Droṇa, foremost in skill, from close at hand struck with his finest shafts those two unconquered best of men who rode together on one car.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca bhojaś ca tathātmajaś ca te; tamonudaṃ vāridharā ivāpatan kṛpasya pārthaḥ saśaraṃ śarāsanaṃ; hayān dhvajaṃ sārathim eva patribhiḥ
english: And Kṛpa, the Bhoja, and your son fell upon him like rain-clouds upon the sun that dispels the dark; but with his shafts Pārtha shattered Kṛpa's bow together with its arrow, his horses, his banner, and his driver.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ praciccheda tavātmajasya; dhvajaṃ dhanuś ca pracakarta nardataḥ jaghāna cāśvān kṛtavarmaṇaḥ śubhān; dhvajaṃ ca ciccheda tataḥ pratāpavān
english: With his arrows he cut down the banner and bow of your roaring son, and the splendid hero slew the fair horses of Kṛtavarman and clove his banner asunder.

sanskrit: savājisūteṣv asanān saketanāñ; jaghāna nāgāśvarathāṃs tvaraṃś ca saḥ tataḥ prakīrṇaṃ sumahad balaṃ tava; pradāritaṃ setur ivāmbhasā yathā tato 'rjunasyāśu rathena keśavaś; cakāra śatrūn apasavyam āturān
english: With their horses and drivers, their bows and their standards, he hastened and slew elephants, horses, and chariots; then your mighty host was scattered and torn through like a dam broken by the flood; and swiftly with Arjuna's chariot Keśava left the afflicted foes upon his left.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāntaṃ tvaritaṃ dhanaṃjayaṃ; śatakratuṃ vṛtranijaghnuṣaṃ yathā samanvadhāvan punar ucchritair dhvajai; rathaiḥ suyuktair apare yuyutsavaḥ
english: Then, as Dhanaṃjaya pressed swiftly onward like the Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices who had slain Vṛtra, other warriors eager for battle pursued him once more on well-yoked chariots with banners raised high.

sanskrit: athābhisṛtya prativārya tān arīn; dhanaṃjayasyābhi rathaṃ mahārathāḥ śikhaṇḍiśaineyayamāḥ śitaiḥ śarair; vidārayanto vyanadan subhairavam
english: Then the great chariot-warriors—Śikhaṇḍin, the grandson of Śini, and the twins—came up to ward off those foes from Dhanaṃjaya's car, and rending them with sharp arrows they shouted most terribly.

sanskrit: tato 'bhijaghnuḥ kupitāḥ parasparaṃ; śarais tadāñjogatibhiḥ sutejanaiḥ kurupravīrāḥ saha sṛñjayair yathā;surāḥ purā devavarair ayodhayan
english: Then in their wrath they smote one another with straight-flying, keen-edged arrows—the Kuru heroes together with the Sṛñjayas—even as of old the Asuras fought against the foremost of the gods.

sanskrit: jayepsavaḥ svargamanāya cotsukāḥ; patanti nāgāśvarathāḥ paraṃtapa jagarjur uccair balavac ca vivyadhuḥ; śaraiḥ sumuktair itaretaraṃ pṛthak
english: Longing for victory and eager to go to heaven, O scorcher of foes, elephants, horses, and chariots fell; they roared aloud, and mightily, each apart, they wounded one another with well-loosed arrows.

sanskrit: śarāndhakāre tu mahātmabhiḥ kṛte; mahāmṛdhe yodhavaraiḥ parasparam babhur daśāśā na divaṃ ca pārthiva; prabhā ca sūryasya tamovṛtābhavat
english: When the great-souled warriors had wrought a darkness of arrows upon one another in that mighty fray, the ten quarters and the heavens themselves grew dim, O king, and the radiance of the sun was wrapped in gloom.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājan kurūṇāṃ pravarair balair bhīmam abhidrutam majjantam iva kaunteyam ujjihīrṣur dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, Dhanaṃjaya, longing to rescue the son of Kuntī—Bhīma, beset by the foremost forces of the Kurus and as if sinking down—came to his aid.

sanskrit: vimṛdya sūtaputrasya senāṃ bhārata sāyakaiḥ prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya paravīrān dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Crushing with his arrows the army of the charioteer's son, O Bhārata, Dhanaṃjaya dispatched the enemy heroes to the realm of Death.

sanskrit: tato 'syāmbaram āvṛtya śarajālāni bhāgaśaḥ adṛśyanta tathānye ca nighnantas tava vāhinīm
english: Then his nets of arrows, veiling the sky in successive flights, became visible, and others besides, smiting your host.

sanskrit: sa pakṣisaṃghācaritam ākāśaṃ pūrayañ śaraiḥ dhanaṃjayo mahārāja kurūṇām antako 'bhavat
english: Filling with his arrows the sky thronged with flocks of birds, Dhanaṃjaya, O great king, became as the End-Maker to the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato bhallaiḥ kṣurapraiś ca nārācair nirmalair api gātrāṇi prākṣiṇot pārthaḥ śirāṃsi ca cakarta ha
english: Then with broad-headed shafts, razor-arrows, and bright iron darts Pārtha wasted their limbs and severed their heads.

sanskrit: chinnagātrair vikavacair viśiraskaiḥ samantataḥ patitaiś ca patadbhiś ca yodhair āsīt samāvṛtam
english: On every side the field was strewn with warriors—limbs hewn off, armor stripped away, heads gone—both with the fallen and with those still falling.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaśarābhyastaiḥ syandanāśvanaradvipaiḥ raṇabhūmir abhūd rājan mahāvaitaraṇī yathā
english: With chariots, horses, men, and elephants struck down by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, the field of battle, O king, became like the great Vaitaraṇī river.

sanskrit: īṣācakrākṣabhaṅgaiś ca vyaśvaiḥ sāśvaiś ca yudhyatām sasūtair hatasūtaiś ca rathaiḥ stīrṇābhavan mahī
english: The earth was strewn with the chariots of the combatants—their poles, wheels, and axles broken, some without horses, some still with their horses, some with their drivers and some with drivers slain.

sanskrit: suvarṇavarmasaṃnāhair yodhaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ āsthitāḥ kṛtavarmāṇo bhadrā nityamadā dvipāḥ kruddhāḥ kruddhair mahāmātraiḥ preṣitārjunam abhyayuḥ
english: Mounted by warriors in golden mail and corselets and decked with gold, noble elephants of perpetual rut, armored and enraged, urged on by enraged drivers, advanced against Arjuna.

sanskrit: catuḥśatāḥ śaravarṣair hatāḥ petuḥ kirīṭinā paryastānīva śṛṅgāṇi sasattvāni mahāgireḥ
english: Four hundred of them, slain by the showers of arrows of the Diademed One, fell down like the living-creatured peaks of a great mountain hurled to the ground.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaśarābhyastaiḥ stīrṇā bhūr varavāraṇaiḥ abhipede 'rjunaratho ghanān bhindann ivāṃśumān
english: The earth strewn with the finest elephants laid low by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, Arjuna's chariot pressed on like the sun cleaving through the massed clouds.

sanskrit: hatair gajamanuṣyāśvair bhagnaiś ca bahudhā rathaiḥ viśastrapatrakavacair yuddhaśauṇḍair gatāsubhiḥ apaviddhāyudhair mārgaḥ stīrṇo 'bhūt phalgunena vai
english: With slain elephants, men, and horses, with chariots shattered in many ways, with valiant fighters whose weapons, plumes, and armor were gone and whose breath had fled, with weapons cast away, the path was strewn over by Phalguna.

sanskrit: vyasphūrjayac ca gāṇḍīvaṃ sumahad bhairavasvanam ghoro vajraviniṣpeṣaḥ stanayitnor ivāmbare
english: And the Gāṇḍīva thundered with a great and terrible sound, dread as the crash of the thunderbolt of a storm in the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādīryata camūr dhanaṃjayaśarāhatā mahāvātasamāviddhā mahānaur iva sāgare
english: Then the host, struck by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, was torn asunder, like a great ship lashed by a mighty gale upon the sea.

sanskrit: nānārūpāḥ praharaṇāḥ śarā gāṇḍīvacoditāḥ alātolkāśaniprakhyās tava sainyaṃ vinirdahan
english: Arrows of many forms, striking weapons sped from the Gāṇḍīva, like firebrands, meteors, and thunderbolts, consumed your army utterly.

sanskrit: mahāgirau veṇuvanaṃ niśi prajvalitaṃ yathā tathā tava mahat sainyaṃ prāsphurac charapīḍitam
english: As a bamboo grove ablaze by night upon a great mountain, so your mighty army flared and quivered, tormented by his arrows.

sanskrit: saṃpiṣṭadagdhavidhvastaṃ tava sainyaṃ kirīṭinā hataṃ pravihataṃ bāṇaiḥ sarvataḥ pradrutaṃ diśaḥ
english: Crushed, burned, and shattered by the Diademed One, your army, smitten and stricken by his arrows, fled on every side to all the quarters.

sanskrit: mahāvane mṛgagaṇā dāvāgnigrasitā yathā kuravaḥ paryavartanta nirdagdhāḥ savyasācinā
english: As herds of deer seized by a forest fire in the great wood, so the Kurus, scorched by Savyasācin, turned and wheeled about.

sanskrit: utsṛjya hi mahābāhuṃ bhīmasenaṃ tadā raṇe balaṃ kurūṇām udvignaṃ sarvam āsīt parāṅmukham
english: For when they had let go the mighty-armed Bhīmasena in that battle, the whole army of the Kurus, panic-stricken, turned its back in flight.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuruṣu bhagneṣu bībhatsur aparājitaḥ bhīmasenaṃ samāsādya muhūrtaṃ so 'bhyavartata
english: Then, when the Kurus were broken, the unvanquished Bībhatsu came up to Bhīmasena and lingered with him for a while.

sanskrit: samāgamya sa bhīmena mantrayitvā ca phalgunaḥ viśalyam arujaṃ cāsmai kathayitvā yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Having joined Bhīma and taken counsel with him, Phalguna told him that Yudhiṣṭhira was free of his arrow and healed of his pain.

sanskrit: bhīmasenābhyanujñātas tataḥ prāyād dhanaṃjayaḥ nādayan rathaghoṣeṇa pṛthivīṃ dyāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then, with Bhīmasena's leave, Dhanaṃjaya went forth, making earth and heaven resound with the thunder of his chariot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ parivṛto bhīmair daśabhiḥ śatrupuṃgavaiḥ duḥśāsanād avarajais tava putrair dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya was surrounded by ten terrible bull-like foes, your sons, the younger brothers of Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: te tam abhyardayan bāṇair ulkābhir iva kuñjaram ātateṣv asanāḥ krūrā nṛtyanta iva bhārata
english: With drawn bows, cruel, as if dancing, O Bhārata, they assailed him with arrows as men torment an elephant with firebrands.

sanskrit: apasavyāṃs tu tāṃś cakre rathena madhusūdanaḥ tatas te prādravañ śūrāḥ parāṅmukharathe 'rjune
english: But the slayer of Madhu kept them upon the left with his chariot's wheeling; then those heroes fled, even while Arjuna's car was turned away from them.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ ketūn rathāṃś cāpāni sāyakān nārācair ardhacandraiś ca kṣipraṃ pārtho nyapātayat
english: As they rushed on, Pārtha swiftly brought down their banners, chariots, bows, and arrows with iron shafts and crescent-headed darts.

sanskrit: athānyair daśabhir bhallaiḥ śirāṃsy eṣāṃ nyapātayat roṣasaṃraktanetrāṇi saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhāni bhūtale tāni vaktrāṇi vibabhur vyomni tārāgaṇā iva
english: Then with ten more broad-headed shafts he struck off their heads to the ground—their eyes red with wrath, their lips bitten through; and those faces shone in the sky like clusters of stars.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu bhallair mahāvegair daśabhir daśa kauravān rukmāṅgadān rukmapuṅkhair viddhvā prāyād amitrahā
english: Having pierced those ten Kauravas with golden armlets with ten swift broad-headed shafts feathered with gold, the slayer of foes passed on.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ tu yāntaṃ mahāvegair aśvaiḥ kapivaradhvajam yuddhāyābhyadravan vīrāḥ kurūṇāṃ navatī rathāḥ parivavrur naravyāghrā naravyāghraṃ raṇe 'rjunam
english: Saṃjaya said: As he who bore the banner of the chief of apes rode on with swift-coursing horses, ninety chariot-heroes of the Kurus charged forth to battle; those tigers among men encircled the tiger among men, Arjuna, in the fray.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaḥ śvetān mahāvegān aśvān kanakabhūṣaṇān muktājālapraticchannān praiṣīt karṇarathaṃ prati
english: Kṛṣṇa urged the white, swift horses, decked with gold and covered with nets of pearls, toward Karṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇarathaṃ yāntam arīn ghnantaṃ dhanaṃjayam bāṇavarṣair abhighnantaḥ saṃśaptakarathā yayuḥ
english: Then, as Dhanaṃjaya rode toward Karṇa's chariot, slaying his foes, the chariots of the Saṃśaptakas advanced, smiting him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇāṃs tu tān sarvān sasūteṣvasanadhvajān jaghāna navatiṃ vīrān arjuno niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But all those ninety heroes, hastening on with their drivers, bows, and banners, Arjuna slew with his whetted arrows.

sanskrit: te 'patanta hatā bāṇair nānārūpaiḥ kirīṭinā savimānā yathā siddhāḥ svargāt puṇyakṣaye tathā
english: Slain by the arrows of many forms loosed by the Diademed One, they fell as Siddhas with their celestial cars fall from heaven when their merit is spent.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvāḥ kuravaḥ kurusattama nirbhayā bharataśreṣṭham abhyavartanta phalgunam
english: Then the Kurus, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, fearlessly bore down, O best of the Kurus, upon Phalguna, the foremost of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tad āyastam amuktāstram udīrṇavaravāraṇam putrāṇāṃ te mahat sainyaṃ samarautsīd dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: That great army of your sons—strained to the utmost, its weapons not yet spent, its mighty elephants reared up—Dhanaṃjaya held in check.

sanskrit: śaktyṛṣṭitomaraprāsair gadānistriṃśasāyakaiḥ prācchādayan maheṣvāsāḥ kuravaḥ kurunandanam
english: With spears, lances, javelins, and darts, with maces, swords, and arrows, the great-bowed Kurus overspread the delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tāṃ kurūṇāṃ pravitatāṃ śastravṛṣṭiṃ samudyatām vyadhamat pāṇḍavo bāṇais tamaḥ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: That outspread and upraised rain of weapons of the Kurus the Pāṇḍava scattered with his arrows, as the sun dispels the darkness with its rays.

sanskrit: tato mlecchāḥ sthitair mattais trayodaśaśatair gajaiḥ pārśvato 'bhyahanan pārthaṃ tava putrasya śāsanāt
english: Then the Mlecchas, with thirteen hundred elephants in rut held ready, smote Pārtha upon his flank at the command of your son.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācais tomaraiḥ prāsaśaktibhiḥ kampanair bhiṇḍipālaiś ca rathasthaṃ pārtham ārdayan
english: With barbed shafts, reed-arrows, and iron darts, with lances, javelins, and spears, with kampana-missiles and bhiṇḍipāla-slings, they harried Pārtha as he stood upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tām astravṛṣṭiṃ prahitāṃ dvipasthair yavanaiḥ smayan ciccheda niśitair bhallair ardhacandraiś ca phalgunaḥ
english: That rain of weapons hurled by the Yavanas mounted on elephants, Phalguna, smiling, cut to pieces with his whetted broad-headed and crescent-headed shafts.

sanskrit: atha tān dviradān sarvān nānāliṅgair mahāśaraiḥ sapatākān sahārohān girīn vajrair ivābhinat
english: Then all those elephants, with their banners and their riders, he pierced with great arrows of many kinds, as the thunderbolt cleaves the mountains.

sanskrit: te hemapuṅkhair iṣubhir ācitā hemamālinaḥ hatāḥ petur mahānāgāḥ sāgnijvālā ivādrayaḥ
english: Studded with gold-feathered arrows, garlanded as if with gold, those great elephants fell slain like mountains crowned with flames of fire.
